Eleven genes show concordant up-regulation across all three molecular levels (cervical spinal cord transcriptome, spinal cord proteome, and CSF proteome) in ALS versus control, with no genes concordantly down-regulated across all three.

The 11 concordant genes, ranked by transcriptomic significance:

1. GPNMB — RNA log2FC=2.653 (adj.P=4.2e-16), SP log2R=0.951 (p=5.4e-06), CSF log2R=3.530 (p=1.3e-03)
2. HLA-DRA — RNA log2FC=1.216 (adj.P=5.1e-13), SP log2R=0.518 (p=4.8e-02), CSF log2R=1.336 (p=7.9e-05)
3. LGALS3 — RNA log2FC=1.361 (adj.P=4.4e-12), SP log2R=0.486 (p=6.7e-03), CSF log2R=1.769 (p=2.9e-04)
4. CAPG — RNA log2FC=1.345 (adj.P=9.0e-12), SP log2R=0.509 (p=1.0e-04), CSF log2R=1.088 (p=2.0e-04)
5. S100A11 — RNA log2FC=1.026 (adj.P=1.8e-09), SP log2R=0.446 (p=1.9e-02), CSF log2R=0.939 (p=1.4e-03)
6. SERPINA3 — RNA log2FC=1.506 (adj.P=2.4e-06), SP log2R=0.640 (p=9.5e-05), CSF log2R=1.591 (p=5.7e-03)
7. EMILIN1 — RNA log2FC=0.594 (adj.P=1.7e-04), SP log2R=0.254 (p=4.7e-02), CSF log2R=1.853 (p=2.6e-02)
8. ICAM1 — RNA log2FC=0.671 (adj.P=2.3e-04), SP log2R=0.444 (p=1.7e-03), CSF log2R=0.932 (p=1.7e-02)
9. SFN — RNA log2FC=1.574 (adj.P=2.7e-04), SP log2R=0.420 (p=1.1e-02), CSF log2R=0.612 (p=6.3e-03)
10. AHNAK — RNA log2FC=0.322 (adj.P=8.0e-03), SP log2R=0.457 (p=2.6e-02), CSF log2R=1.047 (p=1.8e-02)
11. FLNA — RNA log2FC=0.341 (adj.P=1.5e-02), SP log2R=0.464 (p=2.7e-03), CSF log2R=1.012 (p=5.0e-03)

Four genes survive a stricter p<0.01 threshold at all three levels, representing the highest-confidence core candidates: GPNMB, CAPG, LGALS3, and SERPINA3.

GPNMB stands out as the top-priority CSF biomarker candidate: it is the most statistically significant gene in the spinal cord transcriptome (adj.P = 4.16e-16), shows the largest CSF protein elevation (log2R = 3.530, ~11.6-fold increase), and its near-zero change in asymptomatic C9orf72 carriers (spinal cord log2R = 0.025) indicates disease-activity-dependent regulation rather than a genetic-background effect.

Three genes — NEFM, NEFH, and EIF4G3 — were significant in all three datasets but discordant in direction (RNA down, tissue protein up, CSF protein down for neurofilament genes), reflecting the known ALS pathological dissociation between neurofilament mRNA suppression and protein aggregation.

The concordant gene set is dominated by neuroinflammation and glial activation markers (GPNMB, HLA-DRA, LGALS3, CAPG), consistent with the known central role of microglial and astrocyte activation in ALS spinal cord pathology. These genes are biologically plausible non-invasive CSF biomarkers reflecting the neuroinflammatory component of ALS disease activity.
